speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy; could you tell me specifically what kind of feeding difficulties you are experiencing, such as choking, coughing, or refusing to feed?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Are there any episodes of bilious (green) vomiting or "currant jelly" stools, and has the baby passed gas or had a bowel movement since the symptoms started? I also need to request an Abdominal_X-Ray to check for obstruction or volvulus.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray. Given the severe abdominal tenderness and distension in an 8-month-old without vomiting, I need to rule out intussusception immediately, so please also request IMAGES showing an ultrasound of the abdomen.
